title: The Wreck of the Costa Concordia
summary: Hosts Josh and Chuck cover the January 2012 wreck of the Costa Concordia off the Italian island of Giglio: the captain's unauthorized sail-by, the rock strike, the delayed call for help, the captain abandoning ship, the chaotic evacuation and heroes who gave up life jackets, the 2013 parbuckling salvage that righted the ship, its scrapping, the trial and sentences, Costa Cruises' settlements, and the costs. The episode closes with a listener mail from a physician about pain terminology in elderly patients.

segments.title: Tour dates and promotion
segments.summary: Hosts promote their January Pacific Northwest and Northern California tour dates and ticket links.

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Hosts joke about maritime disasters and introduce the Costa Concordia wreck as a modern disaster comparable to the Titanic.

segments.title: The ship and the sail-by of Giglio
segments.summary: The Costa Concordia, launched in 2005 and the largest ship in the Mediterranean, sets out on January 13, 2012. Captain Francesco Schettino sails unusually close to the island of Giglio as a sail-by, partly to honor a retired captain, a maître d' from the island, and to thrill passengers.

segments.title: Captain's affair and motives
segments.summary: Hosts describe the reasons given for the sail-by and the affair between Schettino and Domnica Cemortan, a passenger on board, which prosecutors argued was a motive.

segments.title: Striking the rocks
segments.summary: While performing the close sail-by, the ship hits rocks near Giglio at about 9:45 PM, tearing a 174-foot gash in the port side. A miscommunication with the helmsman and an attempted course correction are discussed, along with expert opinion that the correction would not have mattered.

segments.title: Flooding, power loss and listing
segments.summary: The breach floods the engine room and cuts power. The ship drifts toward shore and comes to rest listing about 70 degrees, a key factor in the death toll. Debate continues over whether Schettino's steering helped.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Ad break.

segments.title: Delayed distress call and abandoning ship
segments.summary: The coast guard is called at 10 PM, but Schettino downplays the situation. Costa Cruises' crisis coordinator Roberto Ferrarini is recorded in calls. Rescue boats arrive around 10:40 PM, and Schettino abandons ship at 11:20 PM, later claiming he fell into a lifeboat. Crew handled lifeboats poorly, and the mandatory drill had not been done.

segments.title: Chaos inside the listing ship
segments.summary: Passengers faced a tilted interior where walls became floors. Coast guard captain Gregorio De Falco ordered Schettino to return to the ship, with the line 'get back on board, damn it.' Twenty-five patrol boats, fourteen merchant vessels and helicopters were on scene by 12:40 AM.

segments.title: Lifeboats and deaths
segments.summary: Twenty-three of twenty-six lifeboats launched, but the disorderly evacuation and the sudden shift to 70 degrees trapped people inside the ship. Thirty-two people died.

segments.title: Crew and passenger heroes
segments.summary: Hosts describe crew members who gave up life jackets, including drummer Giuseppe Girolamo and bartender Erica Sanchez Molina, and the efforts of deputy mayor of Giglio Mario Pellegrini and chief navigator Simone Canessa to lead rescues using a ladder and rope to exit the hull.

segments.title: Injuries and environmental threat
segments.summary: About 150 people were injured, 65 seriously. The ship carried around 2,600 tons of fuel and oil, raising fears of an environmental disaster in the Pelagos Sanctuary, where fishing on Giglio was threatened.

segments.title: Search for remains and survivors
segments.summary: Divers searched the dangerous wreckage for remains. Three people were found alive, including the ship's purser and a honeymooning Korean couple. Two bodies remained missing for a time.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Ad break.

segments.title: Parbuckling salvage operation
segments.summary: Starting in September 2013, engineers used parbuckling, rolling the ship back upright with steel cables and underwater platforms, over the earlier proposal to cut it apart. Monitoring used lasers and microphones, and the ship was then towed away.

segments.title: Recovery of remains and scrapping
segments.summary: Remains of Maria Grazia Trecarichi were found after the ship was upright. Russell Rebello, a waiter who gave away his life jacket, was not found until the ship was being scrapped in Genoa.

segments.title: Legal fallout and trial
segments.summary: Schettino was placed under house arrest, and four crew members pleaded guilty to manslaughter. Schettino went to full trial, was sentenced to sixteen years, which was upheld on appeal in 2017 and he is serving it.

segments.title: Costa Cruises settlements and costs
segments.summary: Costa Cruises faced criticism over language barriers, drills, and open watertight doors. It offered passengers 11,000 euros each in exchange for waiving lawsuits and paid Italy a one million euro fine. The salvage cost about 1.2 billion dollars and the ship was worth about half a billion. Calabrian mafia cocaine reportedly on board.

segments.title: Diver death and De Falco quote
segments.summary: One Spanish diver died during salvage in February 2014. Hosts repeat De Falco's line that Schettino may have saved himself from the sea but he would pay.

segments.title: Further resources
segments.summary: Hosts recommend the Nova documentary on the salvage and a Vanity Fair article about the wreck.

segments.title: Listener mail from a physician
segments.summary: A Michigan physician writes that the show's pain-scale episodes helped him learn that elderly patients may describe pain as soreness, and that the show helps him explain medical topics to patients.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts invite listener email and close the show.
